readings.title: The wet wall
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Residents measured rainfall with identical gauges. One garden consistently reported less than nearby gardens. The coordinator visited and found the gauge beside a wall under climbing plants. After it was moved to an open area, its readings became closer to the others. Earlier records were retained with a note about the location. The coordinator explained that identical instruments did not guarantee comparable observations when the conditions around them differed.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: A blank box in the calendar
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A volunteer missed three mornings of stream observations while caring for a relative. She was tempted to fill the empty boxes using a nearby group's figures. Instead, she marked them 'not observed'. The project leader thanked her: copied figures would falsely suggest independent evidence. A gap limited what researchers could conclude, but an invented observation could mislead them. The project later arranged optional partners to cover absences without changing the meaning of a recorded observation.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: A count at the same hour
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A park group counted cyclists one sunny afternoon and announced that cycling had doubled since winter. A librarian asked whether the winter count had used the same weekday and hours. It had been taken on a rainy weekday morning. The group withdrew the comparison and planned counts at matching times over several weeks. Their first count was still a useful description of that afternoon; it simply could not carry the larger conclusion they had attached to it.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: The photograph with its context
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A volunteer uploaded a close photograph of a damaged leaf. The image was sharp, but the plant could not be identified because no whole-plant view was included. A botanist asked for a second photograph and the date and location. The project then added a short checklist to its submission page. More detail did not mean asking volunteers to write a scientific paper. It meant collecting the small pieces of context that made an observation interpretable.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into natural Chinese, preserving its meaning and logical connections.

A careful observer records not only what was seen but also when and where it was seen. These details help other people judge whether two observations can reasonably be compared. Missing information should remain visible. An honest description of a limitation can be more useful than a confident statement that the evidence does not support.
translation.referenceAnswer: 细心的观察者不仅记录看到了什么，还记录何时、何地看到的。这些细节帮助其他人判断两次观察是否能够合理地比较。缺失的信息应明确保留。坦诚说明局限，可能比作出证据无法支持的自信断言更有用。
translation.explanation: 参考译文不是唯一答案；信息完整、逻辑准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 words in English for this original simulation task.

A neighbourhood science group wants volunteers to record rainfall. Write a short guide explaining how to keep observations consistent, handle missed days, and report unusual readings.
writing.sampleAnswer: To make our rainfall records useful, volunteers should place gauges in open locations and read them at the same agreed time each morning. Please record the date, amount and any change near the instrument, such as new plant growth. If you miss a day, mark it as unobserved instead of copying another garden's figure. A partner may help during planned absences, provided the observer is identified. Unusual readings should be kept with an explanation of anything that might have affected them. Contact the coordinator if you suspect an equipment problem. Our purpose is to describe what we actually observed. A clear note about uncertainty gives the group more useful information than a number invented to fill a box.
writing.explanation: 范文展示一种可行的回应；允许不同观点和例子，按任务完成、组织和语言评分。
